title: Plugin capability manifest
description: The output of plugin-validation's Phase-1 (deep characterization): one document per characterized plugin. INPUTS: an agent-driven read of that plugin's actual files. OUTPUTS, each read by a named downstream consumer: `surfaces` (every contributed surface plus its declared trigger, cited to a real file) feeds Phase 2 (deterministic conform) and Phase 3 (behavioral) case derivation; `could_not_determine` names what the read could not establish, so a downstream tier treats it as an open gap rather than a silent pass; `coverage.manifest_case_ids` is the manifest side of `coverage = manifest - executed` (set difference), the executed side (`coverage.executed_case_ids`) being written back by the tier(s) that ran cases against this manifest. INVARIANTS: (1) Every surface entry carries a `citation` into the plugin's own files - a surface asserted with no citation is not characterization, it is a guess. (2) A could-not-determine gap is first-class: an aspect the read could not establish is named here, never omitted and never asserted as a surface anyway. (3) A weak spot is analytically derived: its `basis` states the reasoning that produced it, not just the conclusion. (4) `coverage.manifest_case_ids` and `coverage.executed_case_ids` are disjoint tracking sets belonging to one document so a downstream consumer can compute the set difference without a second document; neither field is itself the computed coverage. (5) A missing or unreadable manifest is a packaging defect for its consumer, never a signal that the plugin has no surfaces.

schema.description: This manifest schema's version, pinned so a consumer can refuse a document from a schema it does not yet support.

generated_at.description: When this manifest was produced, RFC 3339.

generator.description: What produced this manifest. Optional: a manifest hand-authored for a fixture or golden example carries no generator.

surfaces.description: Every surface the plugin contributes, one entry per surface. An empty array is a claim (this plugin contributes nothing), not the absence of characterization - a plugin with unexamined surfaces reports them in `could_not_determine` instead.

could_not_determine.description: Every aspect the characterization read could not establish - about a candidate surface, a trigger, or a weak spot. Required and explicit: absence of an entry here is a claim that nothing was left undetermined, never the default silence.

identifier.description: Dotted lowercase id, stable within one manifest document.

path.description: Repo-qualified path from the platform root - the first segment names the checkout it resolves in (e.g. `marketplace/plugins/...`). A checkout-relative path would resolve differently for each reader.
Repo-qualified path to the plugin's root directory. Every `citation.path` in this document must resolve inside this path.

marketplace.description: The marketplace catalog this plugin is registered in, if any.

commit.description: The plugin repo commit this manifest was read against, when known.

declared_version.description: The plugin's own `plugin.json` `version` at the cited commit, when known.

tool.description: The characterization engine or author that produced this manifest, e.g. `anthropic-tools/validate-characterize` or `hand-authored`.

model.description: Pinned model ID that ran the characterizing read, when the generator is agent-driven.

citation.description: The evidence for a claim: a real file inside the characterized plugin. Every surface and every weak spot carries one; a gap carries the citation of where the read looked, if it looked anywhere, under `attempted_citation`.

path.description: Repo-qualified path to the plugin file backing this claim.

lines.description: [start, end], 1-indexed, inclusive. Omitted when the claim is about the whole file (e.g. an entire SKILL.md is the skill's trigger description).

excerpt.description: A short verbatim quote from the cited lines, when quoting the exact text materially supports the claim (e.g. a hook `matcher` or a skill's trigger phrase).

surface.description: One capability the plugin contributes: what it is, what invokes it, and the file that proves both.

type.description: The kind of surface, per Claude Code's plugin component model.

name.description: The surface's own declared name (a command name, a skill name, a hook event, an agent id). Required in practice for every type except `other`; left absent only when the plugin's own file gives the surface no name to cite.

trigger.description: What invokes this surface, stated as the declared condition: a hook's event plus matcher, a skill's description-based trigger class, a command's invocation name, an agent's routing description. Read from the plugin's own files, never inferred from the surface's name alone.

weak_spots.description: Analytically-derived concerns about this surface: where its trigger is ambiguous, narrower or wider than intended, unreachable, or otherwise likely to misfire - derived from reading the surface, never from running it (that is Phase 2/3's job).

case_ids.description: Ids of the validation cases downstream tiers derive from this surface. Empty at manifest-authoring time before case derivation runs; each id, once minted, is also carried in `coverage.manifest_case_ids`.

weakSpot.description: A concern derived from reading a surface, not from observing it run.

description.description: What could go wrong, stated as the concrete failure mode (e.g. "matcher regex is unanchored and over-broad"), not just "trigger is unclear".

basis.description: The analytical reasoning that produced this finding - what in the cited text supports it. A conclusion with no basis is an assertion, not analysis.

gap.description: An aspect the characterizing read could not establish. First-class: named here rather than folded into a surface as a guess, or silently dropped.

area.description: What the gap is about: a candidate surface, a specific surface's real trigger condition, or a suspected weak spot - named concretely enough that a later tier knows what to re-examine.

reason.description: Why a static read could not settle it, e.g. runtime-dependent behavior, an ambiguous matcher pattern with no static resolution, or a referenced file absent from the checkout. Never "unclear" alone.

attempted_citation.description: Where the read looked before concluding it could not determine the answer, when it looked anywhere.

coverage.description: The two case-id sets whose difference is coverage. `coverage = manifest_case_ids - executed_case_ids` (set difference) is computed by whichever downstream consumer needs it; this document stores both sides, never the computed result.

manifest_case_ids.description: Every case id named in any surface's `case_ids`, at the time this manifest was last written. The manifest side of the coverage difference.

executed_case_ids.description: Case ids a downstream tier (deterministic conform or behavioral) has reported as executed against this manifest. Empty at manifest-generation time; written back as later phases run. Every id here is expected to also appear in `manifest_case_ids` - an executed id absent from the manifest side names a case that outran its own manifest entry.
